title: Hook
text: In a fraction of a second, an octopus can change its skin color, its pattern, and even its texture.
nxt: It can look like swaying seaweed, a mossy rock, or a lump of coral so well that a diver can swim right past. How does it do that?

title: Wired In
text: Many animals change color slowly. Cephalopod camouflage is wired directly into the nervous system.
nxt: When the brain decides to change color, nerve signals travel to the muscles around each chromatophore.

title: The Puzzle
text: Here is the puzzle. Most octopuses appear to be colorblind.
nxt: Their eyes have only one type of light-sensitive pigment, which in most animals means no color vision.
